title: Proteomics of human platelet samples, LC-MSMS
projectDescription: This study evaluates the performance of adapted SPEED (Sample Preparation by Easy Extraction and Digestion) protocols, a simplified, detergent-free approach tailored for various biological matrices, including lysis-resistant samples. All datasets can be found searching for the keyword NKUAProt001.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Platelet samples were frozen prior to processing. Platelet pellets were either snap frozen in liquid nitrogen or immediately frozen at -80°C to evaluate the effect of freezing methods on the ex vivo proteomic composition. After freezing, protein lysis and denaturation were achieved by adding 10-120 μL of TFA, followed by vortexing and neutralization with eight volumes of 2 M tris base. Protein concentration was measured using a Nanodrop device, and a volume corresponding to 2 μg of protein was transferred to a new 0.5-mL microfuge tube. Tris base 0.1 M was added to adjust the final volume to approximately 50 μL.  Reduction and alkylation were performed using TCEP/CAA, followed by trypsin digestion.Peptides were purified using C18 stage tips before LC-MS/MS analysis. Stage tips were conditioned with 250 μL of MeCN, 250 μL of solvent B (40% MeCN with 0.5% acetic acid) followed by 250 μL of solvent A (H₂O with 0.5% acetic acid). Peptides were loaded and washed with solvent A, and final elution was performed with 40 μL of solvent B, then dried, reconstituted in solvent A, and injected for LC-MS/MS analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: The raw data were analyzed using FragPipe v22.0,  using quantification with DIA-NN v1.9.0, in library-free mode. DIA-Tracer was used to enhance feature alignment and quantification consistency across runs. The search included a tolerance for up to four missed cleavages, peptide length ranging from 5 to 30 amino acids and peptide mass ranging from 300 to 5,000 Da. The false discovery rate (FDR) was set to 1%. Data were queried against UP000005640.
